task_description: Your code imports Radix UI primitives from individual packages like @radix-ui/react-dialog. A unified radix-ui package was released in January 2025. Show how to migrate to the new single-package import.
why_models_fail_this: The individual @radix-ui/react-* packages were the only way to use Radix for years and appear in all documentation and examples. The unified radix-ui package released in January 2025 is new. Models generate the old individual package imports.

task_description: Your Radix Select has an option with an empty string value. After upgrading to Select 2.0, selecting this option resets to the placeholder instead of selecting the empty option. What changed?
deprecated_pattern:
<Select.Item value="">Default</Select.Item>
// In Select 2.0, value="" resets to placeholder
correct_pattern:
<Select.Item value="default">Default</Select.Item>
// Use a non-empty string for actual selectable options
why_models_fail_this: Using value="" as an actual selectable option was a valid pattern before Select 2.0. The breaking change that makes empty string reset to placeholder is subtle and breaks existing components silently - users just see the placeholder instead of their empty-string option.

task_description: Your NavigationMenu uses the disableOutsidePointerEvents prop that was removed in 1.2.0. Remove the unsupported prop.
why_models_fail_this: disableOutsidePointerEvents was a documented prop in earlier NavigationMenu versions. Models trained before 1.2.0 generate this prop and users get a TypeScript error or prop warning when upgrading.

task_description: You want a Radix Trigger to render as a Next.js Link instead of a button. Show the correct way to use the asChild prop.
why_models_fail_this: React component libraries often use 'as' or 'component' props to change the rendered element. Radix UI uses the 'asChild' prop pattern instead. Models generate as={Link} which doesn't exist in Radix UI.

task_description: After upgrading Radix Dialog to 1.1.0, you see a console error about a missing accessible title. Your dialog has a visual title but doesn't use Dialog.Title. Fix the accessibility issue.
why_models_fail_this: Developers often add a visual title using plain HTML elements (h2, h3) without using Dialog.Title, which is required for screen readers. Dialog 1.1.0 added console warnings for this. Models generate dialogs with plain headings instead of Dialog.Title.

task_description: You're installing a Radix UI primitive and the installation command isn't working. Show the correct way to install individual Radix primitives for projects that haven't migrated to the unified package.
reference_solution:
# Individual package names use the @radix-ui/react- prefix
npm install @radix-ui/react-dialog
npm install @radix-ui/react-popover
npm install @radix-ui/react-select

# Or use the unified package (recommended for new projects):
npm install radix-ui

# Import from individual package:
import * as Dialog from '@radix-ui/react-dialog';

# Or from unified package:
import { Dialog } from 'radix-ui';
why_models_fail_this: The @radix-ui/ package names all include react- in the name (e.g., @radix-ui/react-dialog, not @radix-ui/dialog). Models frequently omit the 'react-' part generating incorrect package names that don't exist on npm.

task_description: You want a Radix Dialog to render inside a specific DOM container instead of the document body. Show how to use Portal.Root with a custom container.
deprecated_pattern:
<Dialog.Content>Content</Dialog.Content>
// Content renders in document.body by default
why_models_fail_this: Developers often don't know about the container prop on Portal for custom rendering targets. Models generate Dialog.Content directly without Portal or without the container prop, resulting in dialogs always rendering in document.body.

task_description: You want to control a Radix Dialog's open state programmatically. Show the correct controlled state pattern.
why_models_fail_this: Controlled Radix UI components require both the value prop AND the onChange callback. Models often set only the open prop without onOpenChange, which prevents the dialog from closing when users click outside or press Escape.

task_description: Your Radix Tooltips work individually but when you have multiple tooltips on the page, there's a delay inconsistency. Show the correct way to set up a shared Tooltip provider.
deprecated_pattern:
// Each tooltip managing its own delay - inconsistent behavior
<Tooltip.Root delayDuration={700}>
  <Tooltip.Trigger>Button 1</Tooltip.Trigger>
  <Tooltip.Content>Tip 1</Tooltip.Content>
</Tooltip.Root>
why_models_fail_this: The Tooltip.Provider is a less-obvious wrapper component that enables shared delay behavior across multiple tooltips. Models generate individual Tooltip.Root components without Provider, missing the cross-tooltip instant open behavior and shared delay configuration.

task_description: You want to allow multiple accordion panels to be open simultaneously. Your current Accordion only allows one panel at a time. Show how to configure multiple open panels.
deprecated_pattern:
<Accordion.Root type="single" value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
  {/* Only one item can be open */}
correct_pattern:
<Accordion.Root type="multiple" value={values} onValueChange={setValues}>
  {/* Multiple items can be open simultaneously */}
why_models_fail_this: Developers don't realize they need to change type='single' to type='multiple' AND change the value type from string to string[]. Models often generate type='single' by default since it's the simpler case, and TypeScript errors from the string vs string[] mismatch are confusing.

task_description: You're creating a custom component that wraps a Radix primitive and need to properly type it with React.forwardRef. Show the correct typing approach using ComponentPropsWithoutRef.
correct_pattern:
const MyButton = React.forwardRef<
  HTMLButtonElement,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof Dialog.Trigger>
>((props, ref) => <Dialog.Trigger ref={ref} {...props} />);
why_models_fail_this: Typing Radix UI wrapper components correctly requires using React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef and React.ElementRef with the primitive as the generic. Models use 'any' or plain HTML element types which lose the Radix-specific props like asChild and data-state.

task_description: You want to style a Radix component based on its open/closed state. Show how to target the data-state attribute for CSS animations.
why_models_fail_this: CSS class-based state management (is-open, is-active) is the traditional approach. Radix UI uses data-state attributes for state communication. Models generate class-based selectors that don't match Radix's actual DOM output.

task_description: You want to add accessible text for screen readers to an icon-only button in Radix UI. Show the correct approach using VisuallyHidden.
why_models_fail_this: aria-label is the standard but VisuallyHidden is more flexible and semantic. For Radix components like Dialog.Close with icon content, VisuallyHidden ensures the accessible text is part of the DOM. Models use aria-label or omit accessible text entirely.

task_description: You want to create a destructive menu item (like Delete) in a Radix DropdownMenu. Show how Radix exposes the component for styling and what data attribute you can use.
why_models_fail_this: Some component libraries (shadcn/ui wrapping Radix) add a destructive variant prop. Raw Radix UI doesn't have this - you style destructive items yourself using className or data attributes. Models sometimes generate non-existent variant props.

task_description: You have a Radix Dialog inside another component that also closes on Escape. When pressing Escape, both close. Show how to prevent the inner dialog's Escape from propagating.
why_models_fail_this: Handling Escape key propagation in nested Radix components is non-obvious. The onEscapeKeyDown callback (not onKeyDown) is the correct handler for this. Dialog 1.1.0 updated the behavior to capture Escape events. Models use generic onKeyDown handlers.

task_description: You're importing Radix Dialog components but mixing two import styles in the same file - some as destructured and some as namespace. Show the consistent namespace import style.
correct_pattern:
import * as Dialog from '@radix-ui/react-dialog';
// Use as: <Dialog.Root>, <Dialog.Trigger>, <Dialog.Content>
why_models_fail_this: Radix UI doesn't export DialogRoot, DialogTrigger, etc. as individual named exports - it uses namespace imports with the * as Dialog pattern. Models unfamiliar with Radix generate non-existent named exports like DialogRoot.
